text:
jess-support: Escalating ACME case — they report intermittent differing answers for the same chat prompt after last week's routing change. Root ts 1960001111.

jess-support: Sample API call they used:
```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{ "model": "redwood-chat-4", "messages": [{"role":"user","content":"List the termination and refund policy for the service contract."}], "session_id": "acme-session-77" }
```

jess-support: Output A (customer saw): "Termination: 30 days' written notice. Refunds prorated less administrative fee; early termination fee waived if cancellation due to service outage."

jess-support: Output B (later): "To terminate, provide written notice. Refunds processed at next billing close; penalties may apply depending on contract clause."

miguel-ops: Can you provide request_ids and approximate timestamps so I can pull routing traces?

jess-support: Request ids rQ1960001111-a (≈1960001120) and rQ1960001333-b (≈1960001360).

miguel-ops: Runtime snippets for those windows:
```
[1960001120.08] route_eval: preferred_variant=redwood-chat-4
[1960001120.09] pod_alloc: insufficient_quota -> fallback_variant=redwood-chat-4-quant
[1960001360.52] route_eval: preferred_variant=redwood-chat-4
[1960001360.53] policy_apply: cost_fallback_active -> selected_variant=redwood-chat-3-small
```

arun-ml: That indicates cross-variant serving. quantized and smaller variants tend to shorten or reorder clauses — not mere nondeterminism.

devops-bot: deploy: routing-policy/cost-fallback-enabled rolled by @miguel-ops at 1960000000; enabled cost-based fallback for low-priority tenants.

tim-oncall: Short-term: pin the tenant to a single variant or enable session-stickiness from our side. We can apply tenant override while eng-runtime investigates.

jess-support: I told ACME how to set model_version client-side; they asked if we can force-sticky for them and timeline.

miguel-ops: Applied admin override at 1960001800: tenantOverride("acme-tenant-77", { sticky_sessions: true, preferred_variant: "redwood-chat-4" }). Monitoring now — their calls show consistent variant.

jess-support: ACME confirms stabilization. They're okay short-term but want permanent fix and RCA.

arun-ml: Action items:
- eng-ml: run diff/eval across ACME prompt set for redwood-chat-4, redwood-chat-4-quant, redwood-chat-3-small; flag material divergences. (assign: @arun-ml)
- eng-runtime: add safety rule to avoid mixing variants within a session for tenants marked consistency_required; emit metric for intra-session variant swaps. (assign: @miguel-ops)
- support: issue goodwill credit and document workaround. (assign: @jess-support)

arun-ml: Repro plan: replay ACME prompts with session_id=acme-session-77 at 0.5s intervals for 200 requests, log route.variant, response_text, token_count, semantic_hash; surface cases where identical prompt + session produce different semantic_hash.

miguel-ops: Also pushing a telemetry patch to emit session.variant_swap event when route.variant != last_variant for same session_id — will feed alerts and dashboard.

tim-oncall: If runtime can't push config fast, keep tenant override and schedule policy tightening: prefer sticky sessions when session_id present and/or for enterprise tenants.

arun-ml: Early diffs (first 100 runs): variant swap rate ~12%; when swap occurred ~47% phrasing changes, ~6% material fact changes. If quantized variant causes factual differences we'll remove it from fallback whitelist for contract-sensitive tenants.

miguel-ops: Opening follow-up PR to add tenant-level routing policies and default enterprise behavior: no cross-variant within active session.

tim-oncall: We'll include this incident in weekly postmortem and update routing policy docs. Support, log credit and closure steps.

jess-support: Noted. Sent ACME a short update: override applied, monitoring in place, RCA + fix ETA 5 business days. :email:

devops-bot: incident: created INC-1960005; severity: P2; assigned to eng-runtime.

jess-support: Leaving this thread open until eng-runtime confirms permanent policy change and we have an RCA write-up.
